core_obligations: Choose an explicit presentation of S as a localised quotient of a polynomial ring and generators of the relation ideal, and write R itself as a directed colimit of local rings essentially of finite type over Z (proof lines 32584-32594).

Descend the finitely many coefficients to one index, define the approximating local rings as the localisations of the corresponding quotients at the inverse image of the given prime, and leave the verification that the system has the four stated properties to the reader (proof lines 32595-32608).
proof_roadmap: Put the hypothesis into an explicit finite presentation (proof lines 32584-32591).
Descend the finite data to a stage and localise to build the approximations (proof lines 32592-32609).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a local homomorphism which is essentially of finite presentation is the colimit of a directed system of local homomorphisms that are essentially of finite type over Z, with the transition maps presenting each stage as a localisation of the base change of the previous one (statement lines 32562-32582). The proof does not argue by presentability of the category of local rings: it writes down an explicit localised presentation, descends its finitely many coefficients to one index of a colimit presentation of the source, and defines each approximation by localising the corresponding quotient at the inverse image of the given prime (proof lines 32584-32609). The bookkeeping of the localisations so that the fourth property holds is the substance, and the author leaves that verification to the reader. H2.
